column1: # TiDB integrationtest real-SQL corpus: statements lifted from TiDB's own
# integration tests, with the verdict omni/tidb/parser and TiDB v8.5.5 each give
# each one. This is sample 2 of the design's §3.4 real-SQL corpora
# Where pingcap_parser_corpus.tsv is grammar forms tested one at a time and
# pingcap_parser_rest_corpus.tsv is the forms pingcap's own parser tests combine,
# these are the statements people wrote to exercise the TiDB *server* -- the
# closest public stand-in for user SQL. They lean heavily on DML and query
#   omni    accept | reject -- what tidb/parser.Parse does with the statement
#   engine  accept | reject -- whether TiDB v8.5.5 accepts the syntax, via the
#           same PREPARE harness the other corpora use
#   sql     the statement, verbatim, one line
# A gap is a row with omni reject and engine accept; an over-acceptance is the
# reverse and is a bug. Column 2 is measured, never hand-edited: see README.md.
# integrationtest_corpus_oracle_test.go is the only reader; the live engine test
# samples TIDB_CORPUS_N rows while the omni-verdict test reads every row.
# tool (not checked in, like sample 1's). For each file it drops the mysqltest
# directive/comment lines (leading "--" or "#") and the bare mysqltest control
# lines (connection, connect, disconnect, let, echo, ...), runs
# tidb/parser.Split on what remains, and keeps each non-empty segment.
# Deduplicated within this corpus and against pingcap_parser_corpus.tsv and
# pingcap_parser_rest_corpus.tsv. Only single-line statements are kept, as the
# other corpora are: of 47322 non-empty segments, 1236 with an embedded newline
# or tab (multi-line CREATE/INSERT, compound BEGIN/END blocks) and 243 carrying
# a mysqltest $variable are excluded, 18515 are duplicates within this corpus
# and 82 already appear in the other two, leaving 27246 rows.
# Inc.); the rows are test fixtures read at test time, not compiled into omni,
# and add no module dependency. This header is the attribution.
